1. Personal Preference: My true preference order is w > y > x > z
   - I most want school w
   - School y is my second choice
   - x is third
   - z is my least preferred

2. Priority Ranks: I have high priority at w (rank 1) and y (rank 1)
   - This increases my chances at these top two schools
   - Having top priority means I'm more likely to be accepted

3. Competitive Landscape: Most applicants seem to prefer y > x > w > z
   - This suggests competition will be high at y
   - But I have top priority at y, which helps my chances

4. Strategic Ranking: I want to maximize my likelihood of getting a good school
   - By putting w first, I signal my top preference
   - Keeping y second preserves my high-priority status
   - x and z follow in order of my preference

The key is maintaining my options while strategically ordering schools to optimize my match probability.
